name: USGS Earthquake Catalog
operator: US Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
deduplication: One event catalog across contributing networks, formats and mirrors. Shared USGS operator with National Map; do not add independent publisher counts per API/network.

jurisdiction.data_scope: global seismic events; tested USA/India regions
jurisdiction.country_access: managed cloud vantage only, no geolocation guarantee

capabilities: Historical earthquake lookup by UTC time, magnitude and geographic bounds.
Exact native event ID and revised-record timestamp supplied.
Local GeoJSON interpretation preserves [longitude, latitude, depth_km]; coordinates are not cadastral boundaries.

query.authentication: none for these public documented requests
query.cost: No key/account/paid service used; no numeric quota or unlimited-use claim.
query.paging: Documented limit and offset, offset starts at 1; mutable records require duplicate/version checks.

empty_error_observations.empty: Observed HTTP200 GeoJSON FeatureCollection with empty features for historical regional minmagnitude=9.9; documentation describes nodata 204/404. Do not hardcode emptiness to a single status.
empty_error_observations.invalid: HTTP400 for minlatitude=91, diagnostic retained; no empty/success conversion.
empty_error_observations.paging: offset=1 vs offset=2 with orderby=time-asc returned ci38443183 then ci38450263; fixed filters and origin times retained.

licensing: Official documentation expressly describes a programmatic interface and public GET methods. Anonymous requests use no credentials, accounts or paid service. The response contains event metadata and URLs, not an item-specific license. Do not infer all contributor products/photos/maps are public domain or copy full ancillary products. Current redistribution/attribution conditions and quotas need policy evidence.
limitations: Declared sample: ten preselected historical time/rectangle queries, five USA regions and five India regions. English metadata/place labels; scientific coordinates and UTC times. A bounding rectangle is not a political boundary filter. Some supplied Indian place names contain question-mark transliteration artifacts; preserve raw text and coordinates, do not silently correct titles. This does not establish full geographic or small-earthquake completeness.
Scientific estimates and preferred event IDs may be revised; preserve observed update time and capture date.
Ten event queries do not establish whole-catalog coverage or a fully qualified source.
Human-readable event page passed a limited mobile text check; map basemap was not rendered at screenshot capture. Official feed lifecycle link is currently 404.
next_action: Capture feed lifecycle and applicable rights through allowed official routes; finish human-readable access and revision/deletion/maintenance gates. Ten current examples and boundary checks pass; no activation.

identity_and_duplicates.summary: Official USGS Earthquake Catalog / FDSN event service. Preserve preferred native event ID, contributing network/code, associated IDs, origin time and updated timestamp. Contributing networks and duplicate IDs do not become separate origins. USGS National Map is a separate catalog with a shared agency; no claim of two independent USGS operators.

coverage_and_languages.summary: Declared sample: ten preselected historical time/rectangle queries, five USA regions and five India regions. English metadata/place labels; scientific coordinates and UTC times. A bounding rectangle is not a political boundary filter. Some supplied Indian place names contain question-mark transliteration artifacts; preserve raw text and coordinates, do not silently correct titles. This does not establish full geographic or small-earthquake completeness.

query_contract.summary: GET https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query with format=geojson, starttime/endtime ISO8601 UTC, min/max latitude/longitude, minmagnitude, orderby=magnitude, limit=1. Docs support exact eventid, offset starting at 1, updatedafter, count and named formats. Sample parser preserves GeoJSON longitude/latitude/depth-km axis order and native ID/update metadata. Only ten bounded historical searches currently tested; no text/title/author search, maps/layers or property records.

rights_and_cost.summary: USGS-produced data/information is in the U.S. public domain and USGS requests credit. Third-party media/graphics can remain copyrighted; agency logos and personal likeness have separate restrictions. Core event metadata includes network contributors, so this umbrella policy does not settle every contributed product.
open_questions: Reconcile contributor-specific event metadata/product rights; do not inherit a blanket public-domain grant for images, maps or partner products.

facts.unknown: Contributor-specific event/product rights and territorial copyright treatment; numerical quotas not published here.

reader_access.summary: Anonymous core scientific data and exact event Feature were retrieved. A fresh 390×844 WebKit session rendered the Gujarat event page with matching native event, 2001-01-26 UTC time, 23.419°N/70.232°E and 16 km depth, no login prompt, one main landmark, keyboard focus and no page errors/overflow. The screenshot was visually reviewed: text is readable but the map basemap is a gray placeholder at capture. Map rendering, full accessibility, other-country vantage and contributed-product rights remain unverified; no scientific product files or citizen reports fetched.
open_questions: Verify rendered maps and wider accessibility before treating the outbound page as a tested map viewer.
Record applicable metadata/product rights and country availability; a cloud response is not proof of every country.

quality_and_relevance.summary: Ten independent replay queries matched saved native IDs. All ten scouting records passed declared longitude, latitude, UTC time, magnitude and earthquake-type checks. Exact Gujarat ID resolves to a full GeoJSON Feature (77,109 bytes with associated product metadata; no product files fetched). Fixed time-ascending Ridgecrest pages with offsets 1 and 2 returned different IDs in order. Changed magnitude returned HTTP200 FeatureCollection with zero features, despite documented nodata default 204; observed format behavior takes precedence. Invalid minlatitude=91 returned HTTP400 with bounded diagnostic, not an empty success. Raw Indian place transliteration artifacts remain unchanged. Ten sampled event queries do not measure global catalog recall.

operating_limits.summary: Research cap two records/request and 256 KiB, 20 s request timeout, serial robots-aware minimum-three-second pacing, no automatic retries or redirect following. Docs recommend real-time feeds for live displays; this use is bounded historical lookup. Keep observed update timestamp; revisable catalog is not an immutable historical fact snapshot. Officially linked feed lifecycle policy returned HTTP404, retained as a broken policy link. The event-term documentation redirects to the already captured GeoJSON summary contract; it adds no new lifecycle assurance. Do not invent a refresh/deletion policy from a live endpoint.
open_questions: Find a current operator-published lifecycle/revision/deletion policy; the documented feed-policy URL is HTTP404.
Define responsible maintainer and later-day availability/revision checks.
Honor existing robots/access hold for www.usgs.gov policy host until a useful recovery/access trigger; current successful earthquake.usgs.gov queries do not clear that different host.

decision_and_followup.summary: Candidate for C19 scientific datasets and P06/P09 hazard/environmental information. Not geological-map coverage or legal boundary/ownership evidence. No source activation. Continue public policy/access and query benchmarks before any qualification.
open_questions: Finish the rights, reader, reliability and lifecycle gates; retain unsupported modes and country limitations.
